newsitem.title: POLAND: BRE has outperformed market - Daiwa.
newsitem.headline: BRE has outperformed market - Daiwa.

text.p: Daiwa Europe Limited has given Poland's Bank Rozwoju Eksportu SA an "overvalued accumulate" rating, saying the bank significantly outperformed the overall market last year, Daiwa said in a report dated March 3.
"BRE has outperformed the market by a wide margin during the last year and, in our view, the only potential short-term upside could come from speculative trade," the report said.
"In the medium- to long-run, however, we recognise the bank's high profitability, proactive management, and sound strategy," it added.

Daiwa said BRE's relationship with strategic owner Commerzbank was a "textbook example" of successful cooperation between a domestic and foreign bank, providing BRE access to Commerzbank's world-wide client network.
Commerzbank has a 29-percent stake in BRE and permission from Poland's central bank to raise it to 32.9 percent.
Daiwa said BRE had a strong focus and few formidable competitors in its chosen market segment of small and medium enterprises and high net-worth individuals.

But it said BRE was overly reliant on interest income and that its margins would decline with interest rates. It also said the bank's liquidity was falling as the growth rate of its loan portfolio outpaced that of deposits.
Daiwa predicted BRE would boost net profit to 165.2 million zlotys this year and 200.5 million zlotys next year from 134.7 million zlotys in 1996.
The stock's price-earnings ratio would shrink to 9.3 this year and 7.7 next year from 11.5 in 1996.
